name: Ultrashape

lead: UltraShape is a clinic device that uses focused ultrasound to disrupt fat cells in a chosen area without surgery. It was developed by UltraShape Ltd. in Israel and is used to improve body contours in places such as the abdomen, flanks and thighs.

The appearance payoff is a smaller circumference and thinner fat layer in the treated zone. Controlled trials reported reductions of roughly 2 centimetres in treated-area circumference, with good tolerability, while results are described as modest compared with surgery.

paras: A practitioner moves a handpiece over the marked area while ultrasound energy is delivered through the skin, usually over a series of sessions spaced one to several weeks apart. The newer version adds a radiofrequency handpiece to warm the fat first. Sessions can last from about 30 to 90 minutes depending on the area.

Published trials report that treatment was well tolerated, with most subjects reporting no pain and no serious adverse events in the studies cited. Skin redness and swelling were among measured outcomes. The device is regulated as a medical device and its availability varies by country.

angle.text: The device targets local fat deposits such as the abdomen, flanks and thighs, aiming for a measurable reduction in circumference without surgery. Practitioners describe it as contour refinement rather than weight loss.

lead: UltraShape is a non-invasive body-contouring device that uses focused therapeutic ultrasound to disrupt fat cells selectively. The first-generation Contour I system was developed by UltraShape Ltd. in Israel, and the technology was described in preclinical work as non-thermal focused ultrasound causing selective mechanical lysis of adipocytes [1].

In a 2007 study of 30 healthy patients, three treatments at one-month intervals were given to the abdomen, thighs, flanks, inner knees and, for men, breasts, with efficacy judged by ultrasound fat thickness and circumference and weight monitored to separate fat loss from weight change [2]. A controlled multicenter trial of 164 subjects (137 treated, 27 untreated) reported that a single Contour I treatment was safe and well tolerated and produced a mean reduction of about 2 cm in treatment area circumference [3].

Later studies examined shorter intervals, other body areas and combined devices. A study of 25 women in Paris given three abdominal treatments two weeks apart reported mean midline circumference reduced by 2.47 cm by day 14 after the first treatment and no adverse events [4]. A randomised, controlled study on 14 women reported a 22.2 percent reduction in thigh fat thickness by caliper at 16 weeks against the control thigh [5].
infobox: CE-marked early; later FDA-cleared for abdominal fat reduction [5]

paras: The system delivers focused ultrasound through the skin to mechanically disrupt fat cells while aiming to spare surrounding tissue [1]. A technical and preclinical study characterised non-thermal focused ultrasound for selective fat cell disruption [1]. A second-generation device adds a radiofrequency handpiece that raises the temperature of the adipose tissue before focused ultrasound is applied, which the authors say facilitates the mechanical disruption of fat cells [6].

The 164-subject controlled trial reported about 2 cm average reduction in treated circumference after one treatment, measured over 12 weeks, with safety monitoring including serum lipids and liver ultrasound [3]. Shorter-interval treatment in 25 women reduced mean circumference by 2.47 cm by day 14 after the first treatment [4]. The authors of the combined ultrasound and radiofrequency study note that first-generation studies reported average improvements of 0 to 3.95 cm [6].
Thigh treatment in 14 women showed a statistically significant reduction in caliper-measured fat thickness versus control at every time point [5].

Studies describe the treatment as safe and well tolerated [3]. In the Paris study, no adverse events occurred and about 90 percent of subjects reported no pain [4]. The studies cited track pain, edema and erythema as safety measures [5].

Several human studies exist: a 30-patient prospective study [2], a 164-subject controlled multicenter trial [3], a 25-woman shorter-interval study [4], a 14-woman controlled thigh study [5] and a 20-subject trial of the ultrasound and radiofrequency combination in Asians [6]. Reported results are reductions in circumference of about 2 cm and in fat thickness in the treated area.
